enterpriseNetworking.git.howItWorksHypervisor: A clone or git provider API call from a VM first reaches the gitproxy on the tenant's hypervisor. The tenant's git traffic setting decides whether gitproxy fetches from the host directly, through an HTTP proxy, or hands the request to git-manager.

automations.codeStep.contractBody:
$EVENT_FILE     the trigger event (read-only JSON)
$STATE_FILE     your persistent JSON, <=64KB, kept between runs
$LAST_RUN_FILE  what happened to the items you emitted before
                (read-only): {"items": [{"key", "status", "session_id"}]}
$OUTPUT_FILE    your decision — must be written before exit:
  {"run": true}                     proceed to sessions
  {"run": false, "reason": "..."}   skip this run
  {"items": [{...}, {...}]}         one session per item
Items are capped at 10 per run (max 50); extras run next time.
An item's "id" is a unit of work, not an entity: "INC-1" runs once,
ever. Add "version" (e.g. the upstream updated_at) so a reopened item
counts as new work. An item whose session fails is released and can
run again.

Devin creates a Slack app for each {{botName}}. A Slack admin can approve them automatically:
1. In Slack's admin settings, go to Integrations → Installed apps and open Devin.
2. Click Manage → Manage permissions.
3. Check "Allow this app to install managed agent apps", then click Save.

oncall.setup.previewInvestigating: Looking into the transfer errors. I’ll post once I know what’s failing.
oncall.setup.previewFix: Found it: <commitLink>a3f9c21</commitLink> drops the idempotency key on retries. Opened <prLink>PR 74414</prLink> to restore it.
oncall.setup.previewLoginAlert: Login API returning 5xx on more than 10% of requests
oncall.setup.previewLoginInvestigating: On it. Errors started at 10:41, right after the auth-service deploy. Checking if that’s the cause.
oncall.setup.previewLoginFix: Mitigated: rolled auth-service back and logins are succeeding again. <commitLink>e91b7d4</commitLink> broke session token validation; opened <prLink>PR 74502</prLink> to revert it.
oncall.setup.previewBugReport: A few customers are reporting a blank results page on /search. Can someone take a look?
oncall.setup.previewBugInvestigating: Taking a look. Reproducing it, then checking recent changes to the search page.
oncall.setup.previewBugFix: Traced it to <commitLink>c48b1f3</commitLink>, deployed to prod this morning: the new cursor pagination drops the first page when results span more than one shard. Escalating to <mention>@Jake</mention> as the code owner.
oncall.setup.previewDiskPressureAlert: 3 of 12 nodes in prod-us-east above 90% disk
oncall.setup.previewDiskPressureInvestigating: On it. Checking disk usage by path on the affected nodes.
oncall.setup.previewDiskPressureFix: Found it: log rotation stopped when the log-shipper DaemonSet lost its volume mount, so container logs are filling /var/log/pods. Want me to cordon the 3 nodes and clear the backlog?
oncall.setup.previewDiskPressureLabel: Trace root cause down the stack
oncall.setup.previewSlowQueryAlert: p95 query time on GET /graphql/orders above 2s
oncall.setup.previewSlowQueryInvestigating: On it. Pulling the query plan and checking what changed on the orders endpoint.
oncall.setup.previewSlowQueryFix: Found it: Unbounded IN (...) clauses in the list_customers dataloader batched 1500+ conversation IDs, causing multi-second query execution times. Want me to add a batch-size cap or pagination to the dataloader?

See "How to receive webhooks" on this page for a full example.

settings.webhookUrlCreateHint: As soon as you click Create, we POST a signed endpoint.verification event to this URL. Your receiver must respond 2xx with the request's data.nonce in the body before the endpoint goes live — see "How to receive webhooks" for an example
settings.webhookUrlEditHint: Changing the URL sends a new endpoint.verification event to it. Deliveries pause until the new URL responds 2xx with the request's data.nonce
settings.webhookPendingHint: Waiting for this URL to answer the endpoint.verification event with a 2xx that includes data.nonce. No events are sent until it does — click Verify to send the event again.
settings.webhookGuideIntro: Every event is an HTTPS POST with a JSON body and Standard Webhooks signature headers, sent to the URL you register. One handler receives everything and branches on event_type — it only needs to do three things:
settings.webhookGuideStep1Body: When you add an endpoint (or change its URL, re-enable it, or click Verify) we immediately POST an endpoint.verification event whose data.nonce you must echo back: respond 2xx with that exact nonce in the body, e.g. {"nonce": "…"}. This is the only event that needs an echo — every other event just needs a 2xx. Until it passes, the endpoint stays pending and receives no events.
settings.webhookGuideStep2Body: Each request carries webhook-id, webhook-timestamp and webhook-signature headers. Compute HMAC-SHA256 over {webhook-id}.{webhook-timestamp}.{raw body} with your signing secret (base64-decode the part after whsec_) and compare it with the space-separated v1,… values in the signature header — any match is valid, and there are several while a secret rotation is in progress.
settings.webhookGuideStep3Body: Return a 2xx within 10 seconds; anything else is retried with backoff for about three days, after which the endpoint is disabled. Retries and replays reuse the same webhook-id, so treat a repeated ID as already handled.

Personal access tokens are governed separately by the PAT policy. SCIM provisioning and Outpost workers are exempt.
